# libreac / fuzz_grant

libreac's own fuzz target `fuzz_grant` ([source](source/fuzz_grant.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libreac 1.9.0 (FreeREAC/libreac at d16f3f4e).

From the payload, sets head-amp table cells, asks the grant to admit a box at an input-chosen head-amp base and width, builds its enrolment sweep into a buffer of an input-chosen number of rows (its own allocation), builds a sweep for a hand-made allocation, then arms a scene replay over an input-chosen base and width and a re-assert period, and runs the head-amp scheduler for up to 4096 frames.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static libreac.a of every src/*.c of libreac 1.9.0 at commit d16f3f4e, compiled with each build's flags, as libreac's Makefile builds its fuzz targets but with this toolchain in place of a native clang and libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- A head-amp cell is set exactly when its channel and value are legal and then reads back as set, an unknown parameter has no value, and every unset cell carries the stated enrolling default: phantom off, pad off, and a SENS that is not zero ([lines 201-253](source/fuzz_grant.c#L201-L253)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A box is admitted, at the base and width it asked for, exactly when its slots are a positive width of at most REAC_GRANT_MAX_WIDTH inside the head-amp space; a refused one leaves the caller's allocation unchanged ([lines 256-294](source/fuzz_grant.c#L256-L294)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every sweep row is a cd ea link-4 SINGLE block whose bytes from offset 2 sum to zero ([lines 94-113](source/fuzz_grant.c#L94-L113)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A group-A row, framed as a master stamps it, parses back as a HEADAMP record of its channel, parameter and the value the input last set for that cell (or the default), with its record and block checksums closed ([lines 116-170](source/fuzz_grant.c#L116-L170)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A sweep has REAC_GRANT_SWEEP_LEN rows or is refused for a smaller buffer; its two head frames are the measured ones byte for byte, its group-A rows are one per allocated channel per parameter in the measured order, and group B is the identity poll for the addresses and sizes the header names ([lines 301-358](source/fuzz_grant.c#L301-L358)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The sweep builder admits a hand-built allocation on the same terms as reac_grant_allocate and refuses NULL arguments ([lines 373-385](source/fuzz_grant.c#L373-L385)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The head-amp scheduler only emits a channel, parameter and value the table can hold, with the value the input last set (or the default), for a cell the input set or one inside the armed scene, and sends an unset cell at most once ([lines 398-448](source/fuzz_grant.c#L398-L448)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

| statement | in one line | status |
|---|---|---|
| `plain_halts` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2 | [proved](proofs/plain_halts/) |
| `ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2 | [proved](proofs/ubsan_halts/) |

| `asan_ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the ASan+UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2 | [proved](proofs/asan_ubsan_halts/) |
| `asan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/asan_agrees/) |
| `ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; UBSan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/ubsan_agrees/) |
| `asan_ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan+UBSan never fires; memory refused only when forced | [proved](proofs/asan_ubsan_agrees/) |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libreac` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_grant.plain` | 51,888 | `e84d949045ee7d14c479c0745d7b8b59250d878e24e568689ef5f5f23b680a19` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_grant.ubsan` | 54,816 | `ae8453d49b86e32aeb3c7ba4ee8bcda4aba4982505e024338158e8e0ec3a0b15` |
| asan | `fuzz_grant.asan` | 584,312 | `c2c7559b29bdf39cb13acdfb062d6b930efb2b56f84ab4e0c71bd5711d9e015e` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_grant.asan-ubsan` | 587,992 | `fde52226dc48de254681156061de9263409c123ca0a0d6c5010ded4e17f602df` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
